intro: We are a translational neuroscience lab studying the molecular pathways that drive the two most common neurologic disorders — stroke and dementia. Our work spans the vascular biology of the brain, from single glial cells to human clinical biomarkers, with the shared goal of protecting and repairing the brain's white matter.

areas.title: Neurovascular mechanisms of white matter injury & repair
areas.description: White matter is exquisitely vulnerable to vascular injury. We study how signaling between blood vessels and oligodendrocyte lineage cells — the "oligovascular niche" — controls myelin loss and repair after ischemic stroke, including IL-17/CXCL5 chemokine signaling and SARM1-driven axonal degeneration.
highlights: IL-17/CXCL5 signaling in human and mouse white matter injury
SARM1 as a target to limit axonal degeneration

areas.title: Vascular contributions to cognitive impairment & dementia
areas.tagline: How the failing neurovascular unit drives decline
areas.description: An NIA-funded program investigating how vascular dysregulation contributes to neurodegeneration and Alzheimer's disease, including the interplay between neurovascular dysfunction and tau aggregation, and the angiogenic factor placental growth factor (PlGF) as a driver and marker of decline.
highlights: Placental growth factor (PlGF) and cognitive trajectories

areas.title: Intracranial atherosclerotic disease
areas.description: Intracranial atherosclerotic disease is a leading cause of stroke worldwide. We build flow-dependent, endothelialized 3D in vitro models of the cerebral vasculature to dissect disease mechanisms and test therapeutic and endovascular strategies.

areas.title: Blood-based biomarkers & clinical translation
areas.tagline: From the bench to the clinic
areas.description: We develop and validate blood-based biomarkers of cerebral small vessel disease and post-stroke cognitive impairment, partnering in national consortia (MarkVCID) and contributing to AHA scientific statements that shape clinical practice — always with a commitment to equity in science and medicine.
highlights: Inflammatory network biomarkers of stroke risk
AHA scientific statements on vascular brain health
